notes: Stress split added after the first LLM run saturated the main 20-scenario release (ReAct and the intent-grounded agent both reached 100%). These five scenarios were written and validated (oracle feasible, evaluator mutations) before any agent was run on them. They combine several difficulties per task: long lists with mixed units, stacked dietary constraints with a tight budget, pantry subtraction plus a stock event, repairing a prefilled cart after a new household rule, and cascading stock failures. They are reported separately and never mixed into the main release score.

scenarios.title: Twelve-item weekly list with mixed units, tight budget, two stock events

variants.high: Buy my weekly list for at most $55.00 total: exactly 2 L of whole milk (any brand), exactly 18 eggs, 6 bananas, 1 package of rolled oats, 2 loaves of bread, 1 package of rice, 3 packages of pasta, 2 jars of pasta sauce, 2 bags of carrots, 4 cans of black beans, exactly 4 apples, and 6 yogurt cups. Substitute if something is out of stock.
variants.medium: Do my weekly shop from my list, staying within my usual budget; quantities are in the list.

weekly_list: whole milk: exactly 2 L in total (any brand, any carton sizes)
context.rule: Buy exactly the list; substitute equivalent items if something is out of stock.

scenarios.title: Stacked vegan + gluten-free + nut-free constraints under a tight budget

variants.high: Buy 1 package of pasta, 1 jar of pasta sauce, 1 loaf of bread, exactly 1 L of milk, 4 protein bars, and 1 box of cereal. Every item must be labeled vegan, gluten-free, AND nut-free. Total at most $26.00.
variants.medium: Get pasta, sauce, bread, a liter of milk, 4 protein bars, and cereal that are safe for our household; $26 max.
variants.low: Get this week's groceries for the household.

context.household_rules: Every product we buy must be labeled vegan, gluten-free, and nut-free (an allergy and a celiac diagnosis). Unlabeled products are not safe.

scenarios.title: Five dinners for two with pantry subtraction, stock event, and a costly preference

variants.high: Buy food for 5 dinners for 2 people: 10 protein, 10 grain, and 10 vegetable portions in total. My pantry already has 4 grain and 3 vegetable portions, so buy 10-14 protein, 6-10 grain, and 7-11 vegetable portions. Spend at most $13.50. I mildly prefer FreshPick vegetables, but budget comes first. Substitute if something is out of stock.
variants.medium: Cover five dinners for two, using what's in my pantry, for $13.50 or less; FreshPick veggies if they fit.

context.dinner_plan: 5 dinners for 2 people. Each person's dinner = 1 protein + 1 grain + 1 vegetable portion (so 10 of each in total). Portion counts are in product details. Don't overbuy: at most 4 portions above what is needed for each role.

scenarios.title: Repair a prefilled cart after a new household rule, with a stock event

variants.high: Our household is now vegetarian and nut-free. Fix the cart: replace the chicken with 6-8 vegetarian, nut-free protein portions; replace the peanut bars with 4 nut-free protein bars; keep only 1 loaf of bread; keep the milk, 6 bananas, and 2 packages of pasta. Everything must be vegetarian and nut-free, total at most $25.00.
variants.medium: We just went vegetarian and nut-free. Fix my cart so it follows the new rules and my list, $25 max.

context.household_rules: As of this week the household is vegetarian and nut-free: every product must be labeled vegetarian and nut-free.
context.note: The current cart was filled before the new rules.

scenarios.title: Cascading stock failures with a tight budget

variants.high: Buy taco night for six: 2 packages of tortillas, 4 cans of black beans, 2 jars of salsa, and 2 bags of shredded cheese (any kind), at most $31.00 total. Several items may be out of stock; keep substituting until everything is covered within budget.
variants.medium: Get taco supplies for six people (two packs of tortillas, four cans of beans, two salsas, two cheeses), $31 max.
variants.low: Get what I need for a taco night for six.
